newsitem.title: UK: Libya sentences eight to death as spies, CIA links.
newsitem.headline: Libya sentences eight to death as spies, CIA links.

text.p: Libya's top military court has sentenced six senior officers and two civilians to death for spying, using equipment supplied by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), Libyan television reported.
The state-run television said they were convicted of passing defence secrets to foreign governments and belonging to "a banned organisation linked to agents of foreign governments".

The report, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC), did not name the governments but said the convicted men used CIA-supplied equipment and implied they were spying for the United States.

"You mobilised yourselves as spies against your country and allowed the enemies to get hold of military, economic and security capabilities by using sophisticated equipment supplied by the CIA," an unidentified official said.

"Have you forgotten or are you just playing down what those who recruited you as spies, have done to us? They killed our children, tore our bodies apart, raided our families as they were sleeping late in the night," he said, in an apparent reference to the U.S. bombing of Tripoli and Benghazi in 1986.
The report -- a rare public admission of opposition within the military to the rule of Colonel Muammar Gaddafi -- said six other officers and two civilians were acquitted.
Six of those found guilty would be executed by firing squad and two by hanging, it said.

"The Supreme Military Court...has passed its sentences against the agent-spies who sold their honour, dignity and homeland to their enemies and supplied agents of foreign governments with information relating to the country's defence secrets, for espionage purposes, by exploiting their membership of the Libyan army," the Libyan television report said.

The official said the accused men wanted Gaddafi "to be harmed in the vilest operation of history" but it was not clear if the eight men were directly accused of being involved in the 1986 bombing in which Gaddafi's residential compound was hit.

U.S. military aircraft bombed targets in Tripoli and Benghazi on April 15, 1986. Ten days earlier a bomb had exploded in a West Berlin disco, killing a U.S. soldier and a Turkish woman. The United States accused Libya of instigating that incident and other attacks against U.S. targets in the Middle East and Europe.
Libyan television showed pictures of the courtroom where about 12 of the accused could be seen seated in a large cage, the BBC said.
Their heads were shaved and they appeared to be wearing prison uniforms.

Those sentenced to death were named as Colonel Muftah Muhammad Gamum, Staff Colonel Mustafa Abu al-Qasim Masud, Flight Lt-Colonel Sad Salih Faraj, Major Khalil Salim Muhammad, Major Ramadan al-Ihumi Muhammad Ali, and Major Mustafa Hubayl al-Fudhil.
Two civilians, named as Isad Misbah Isad al-Amin and Sulayman Ghayt Muftah, were sentenced to death by hanging.
